decisions.rationale: The fall is explained by fuel-cost fears, not a broken business, and the stock is cheap. But margins sit at a cycle high, the usable EV/EBITDA fair value gives only modest upside to base, the macro tilt is toward bear, and Q3 on Nov 6, 2026 will show whether margins held. Good but not compelling: AVOID, re-research after results.

The entry-price hit reflects de-rating, not a fundamental break, but the price still sits above every mechanical fair value and above its own 5y multiple range, while part of TTM margin is one-off tariff refunds. Good business, not a compelling price: AVOID at conviction 3.

The fall reflects a real Q3 profit slowdown from competition, confirmed by lower TTM margins and halved FCF margin; the cash-conversion trigger has fired. Price equals base fair value, so no margin of safety. Quality is still exceptional, so conviction 3, not lower, but below the buy threshold.

Low multiples and a repaired balance sheet are real, but TTM margins far above any fiscal year look cyclical, base and bear fair values sit well below the price, FCF has been negative in two of the last two fiscal years, and there is no verified moat. Good but not compelling: AVOID, no position.

Quality is metal prices, not a structural edge; multiples are low only on peak earnings, while EV/Sales and P/B sit above their 5y medians and price exceeds base fair value. The macro tilt is mildly negative and NAV is unavailable. Good balance sheet, not a compelling entry: AVOID with an entry price at base fair value less the margin of safety.

Cash generation and balance sheet are strong, but margins are cyclical and gold-driven, there is no discount to peers, price sits far above base fair value, macro tilts small toward bear and results arrive Nov 5. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, no position; re-research at a price that discounts cycle risk.

The quality is cyclical: margins and ROIC track gold, and FY2023 shows how fast they reverse. Low multiples sit on peak earnings, P/B is above its 5y max, the share count is rising, and the macro overlay leans bearish. There is no margin of safety on normalised earnings, so cash is the better choice.

Balance sheet and cash returns are strong, but margins are gold-driven and at a peak. P/E and P/B are rich against peers and its own history, base and bear fair values sit far below the price, and macro tilts toward bear. The risk/reward is skewed to the downside: good, not compelling, so AVOID.

The evidence for value rests on financials that probably describe a larger pre-demerger group, so neither the multiples nor fair value can be trusted. Add cyclical returns and governance/regulatory overhangs, and conviction is low. No position; re-research once post-demerger results (Oct 28) allow a like-for-like valuation.

Strong cash generation and deleveraging are real, but earnings are likely near peak spreads, the only working valuation method puts base value below the price, Q3 2026 results are unread and capex may restart. Good but not compelling, so this is an AVOID. Cash is acceptable.

Returns and the de-rating are striking, but negative FCF for three years, a Piotroski F of 3, dilution and an unexplained 59.6% collapse leave the cheap P/E unbacked by cash. The price is above base fair value, so there is no margin of safety. Good but not compelling: AVOID.

Strong cash conversion and a clean balance sheet, but TTM margins are far above the FY2022-23 trough and the through-cycle DCF base is below the price. Multiples below the 5y minimum reflect peak earnings, not a mispricing. The trend is negative and results are due in days. Good but not compelling: AVOID, with a margin-of-safety entry price.

Quality and balance sheet are strong, but margins sit far above their five-year trough, management expects aluminium to normalize, the price is above base fair value and the macro tilt leans bearish. Good but not compelling: no position. A lower price would give margin of safety against margin normalisation.

The drift catalyst is unverified as a results beat. The volatility stop at 227.71 is far below the close, and the only supported target, the 52-week high of 289.50, gives well under 2:1, while the 362.68 that 2:1 requires has no support. The stock is overbought (RSI 80.6) against a falling 50-day. No position; cash is acceptable.

The ATR stop below the reaction-day low makes the minimum 2:1 target 49.57. That is far above the 52-week high and base fair value, so it depends on the bull case within eight weeks. The entry is overbought after a partly sector-wide jump. The honest target does not reach 2:1, so this is an AVOID with no position.

A bid-driven move is binary deal risk, not drift. The close is above the offer level, so the 2:1 target of 13.84 needs a higher or rival bid that no evidence supports, and a failed approach could gap through the 10.96 stop. The reward:risk does not hold, so this is an AVOID.

The setup's edge is unclear because the beat can't be verified from the evidence. The price is overbought and above every 5y multiple maximum. The rule-based 2:1 target needs a break above the 67,300 high, so reward:risk is not supported. Conviction is 2, so no position.

The drift signal is real, but the only evidenced target, the 198.70 six-month high, gives about 0.9:1 against the ATR-based stop at 161.6; reaching 220.4 needs a breakout that fair value, RSI 78.5 and the downtrend do not support. The rule fails, so AVOID; cash is acceptable.

The drift setup qualifies, but the honest target (bull fair value 132.40) is well short of the roughly 151.2 needed for 2:1 against a stop near 100.54; RSI 87.5 adds gap risk. The trade fails the reward:risk rule, so no position.
